ranked_evidence.title: 'I am still alive': Indian activist on hunger strike for 26 days loses 11kg - BBC
ranked_evidence.snippet: Indian activist and educationist Sonam Wangchuk, who has been on a hunger strike for 26 days in support of the Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), says he has lost 11kg (24lb) but is "still alive". Popularly known as "Sonam sir", Wangchuk has been the main draw at the youth-led movement seeking education reforms and the resignation of Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan. He was forcibly removed from the CJP's protest venue at Delhi's Jantar Mantar on Saturday and taken to hospital from where he continues his fast. Meanwhile, thousands continue to turn up at the protest venue even after the brutal police crackdown on Monday's march to parliament which left dozens of protesters and policemen injured. Modi has not commented directly on the protests or engaged with the protesters, but on Thursday, he posted a statement on X that is being seen as an attempt to reach out to students who have been frustrated with repeated exam paper leaks.

ranked_evidence.title: India’s Cockroach protests: Rahul Gandhi detained after calling for PM Modi to resign - The Guardian
ranked_evidence.snippet: Opposition leader taken away after accusing Narendra Modi of ‘destroying the future of India’s youth’ during protest in solidarity with cockroach movement. Indian police briefly detained opposition leader Rahul Gandhi on Tuesday during protests calling for prime minister Narendra Modi’s resignation, in solidarity with the new youth-led cockroach party movement. Gandhi, the leader of India’s Congress party, staged a sit-in outside Modi’s house on Tuesday afternoon, stating that Modi must resign “for destroying the future of India’s youth”. His protest took place as thousands of students were gathered at a separate site in central Delhi, the day after a huge protest calling for the resignation of Modi’s education minister was met with brutality by Delhi police, including baton attacks and teargas. Gandhi said his party was taking their protest directly to the prime minister’s house, after the Modi government refused to take up the issues of the students and the alleged “brutality unleashed on students” in parliament.

ranked_evidence.title: India’s youth-led Cockroach movement vows to keep demanding reforms after police crackdown - Greenwich Time
ranked_evidence.snippet: # India’s youth-led Cockroach movement vows to keep demanding reforms after police crackdown. NEW DELHI (AP) — Supporters of India’s youth-led Cockroach movement demanding educational reforms and government accountability refused to leave their New Delhi protest site Tuesday, a day after their thousands-strong march toward Parliament drew police tear gas, beatings and a new wave of sympathy from across the country. The movement, now attracting professionals and families beyond students, represents a rare public challenge to Prime Minister Narendra Modi ’s government, reviving criticism over its handling of dissent and use of force to respond to protests. Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi and dozens of his Congress party lawmakers showed their support Tuesday with a sit-in outside Modi’s residence before police forcibly removed them in a dramatic escalation. Government minister Jitendra Singh said Gandhi was told the location was not “suitable for a sit-in.". Ada's coffee and candy shop on course to reopen in Riverside part of Greenwich.
